answer: Each identity claims one grove watch post and locks a 70-credit bond. It pays for a juniper post, keeps its ember fire alight through an assigned window, and gets co-signatures from two neighbors. An auditor checks that no watcher key signed two posts in overlapping windows; any overlap burns bonds. The first post costs 32 credits, the kth costs 32+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5027 and 1000 fakes pay 2,529,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-watch ring fails because one hired watcher cannot stand in two groves at once. An honest agent pays 32 once and keeps its bond after a clean watch.
